note: Task 046a, BIE's toolbox (auzaar-ghar). One entry per library, tool, asset source or dataset that BIE uses to show what a scene plan asks for. A Python library computes, a BIE block shows. Versions are pinned (npm: the newest release before npm_before, the date in tools/npm_before.txt; PyPI: the newest release before the same date with a Python 3.13 Linux wheel). Licences were read from each project's own page or package metadata on 25 October 2026; licence_flags mark share-alike, GPL, custom and per-item licences for Navin's later licence decision, without blocking them. status: installed < wrapped < demo_proven < used_on_real_book; blocked_with_reason says what is missing.

tools.name: BIE block library (bie/brain/video/blocks)
tools.block: image, label, highlight, flow, steps, timeline, scale, table, arrow, question + camera
tools.notes: Task 039's 2D blocks with the camera that zooms into any region of a picture; organ_zoom is an image layer plus camera keys.

tools.name: Remotion
tools.licence: Remotion License: free for individuals and companies of up to 3 people; a paid company licence above that
tools.notes: The video framework every BIE block is written for (useCurrentFrame, interpolate, spring, Sequence, delayRender). Previews and CI demos run the same blocks through remotion-lite (bie/brain/video/preview/remotion-lite.tsx, same API names) in Chromium + ffmpeg; the real Remotion render of the same blocks is the bridge proof. Navin's licence decision is needed before BIE is run by a company of more than 3 people.

tools.name: @remotion/three
tools.notes: ThreeCanvas: a React Three Fiber canvas driven by Remotion's frame clock; remotion-lite has a shim with the same name (bie/brain/video/preview/three-lite.tsx).

tools.name: three.js
tools.notes: WebGL scenes; in headless Chromium it runs on SwiftShader (software WebGL).

tools.name: React Three Fiber
tools.notes: three.js as React components.

tools.name: @react-three/drei
tools.notes: Helpers: glTF loading (useGLTF), environment light, bounds.

tools.name: KaTeX
tools.notes: Typeset maths in the video (fonts bundled into the preview).

tools.name: D3
tools.notes: Scales, axes, paths and layouts for every plotted block, d3-geo for maps (batch 2 and 3), the time scale and the tree layout (batch 3).

tools.name: 3Dmol.js
tools.notes: Molecules (ball and stick, sticks) and proteins (cartoon) from SDF or PDB text.

tools.name: Mol*
tools.notes: The PDB's own viewer; detailed protein surfaces and cartoons for advanced levels.

tools.name: Matter.js
tools.notes: 2D rigid bodies; stepped with a fixed time step from frame 0, so every frame is the same on every render.

tools.name: cannon-es
tools.notes: 3D rigid-body physics computed in the page with a fixed time step; three.js draws it.

tools.name: Blender (bpy, headless)
tools.licence: GPL-3.0-or-later (the program); models BIE makes with it are BIE's own
tools.notes: Route C: Python scripts build 3D models once and export glTF for three.js; Blender also imports FBX/OBJ anatomy models and exports parts as glTF.

tools.name: NumPy
tools.licence: BSD-3-Clause AND 0BSD AND MIT AND Zlib AND CC0-1.0
tools.notes: Arrays for every computed scene.

tools.name: SciPy
tools.notes: ODE solving (a falling body with air drag), signals.

tools.name: SymPy
tools.notes: The checker: every step of an equation on screen is proved equal to the one before, and LaTeX comes from SymPy.

tools.name: Manim (Community Edition)
tools.notes: Renders maths and physics clips where its animation grammar beats the web path; needs Cairo and Pango on the machine. Text-only scenes need no LaTeX.

tools.name: statsmodels
tools.notes: Regression and statistics computed for the scene (the fitted line and R squared shown are statsmodels' own).

tools.name: NetworkX
tools.notes: Graph layouts and traversals (BFS order) for D3 to draw.

tools.name: Biopython
tools.notes: Reads PDB files: chains, residues, the alpha-carbon trace and secondary structure for labels.

tools.name: NeuroKit2
tools.notes: Simulates a realistic ECG and finds its P, QRS and T points.

tools.name: RDKit
tools.notes: Molecules from SMILES with 3D coordinates; reactions from reaction SMARTS; 2D drawings as SVG.

tools.name: Cantera
tools.notes: Reaction kinetics and equilibrium: how the amounts of reactants and products change over time.

tools.name: trimesh
tools.notes: Added by Claude (not in Navin's list): converts OBJ and STL meshes (BodyParts3D, NIH 3D) to glTF without starting Blender, and measures them.

tools.name: Servier Medical Art
tools.notes: Medical illustrations; checked 25 October 2026: single images download as PNG (transparent, about 600 px), vector shapes only inside PowerPoint sets, no SVG files. Credit: 'Servier Medical Art (smart.servier.com), CC BY 4.0'.

tools.name: Z-Anatomy
tools.notes: A whole-body anatomy atlas; the FBX files per body system (for example CardioVascular41.fbx, 65 MB) are fetched on demand and Blender exports the needed part as glTF. Share-alike: a video that adapts it may have to carry the same licence (Navin's decision).

tools.name: BodyParts3D
tools.licence: CC BY 4.0 (licence page read 25 October 2026; releases up to 3.0 were CC BY-SA 2.1 Japan; the page also asks users to contact DBCLS)
tools.notes: Organ meshes named by FMA id inside a 62 MB zip; one part is extracted and converted to glTF with trimesh. Credit: 'BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science licensed under CC Attribution 4.0 International'.

tools.name: NIH 3D
tools.licence: per model (Public Domain / CC0, CC BY and others)
tools.notes: Entry metadata from /api/entries/<id>, the file from /api/download?submissionId=..&fileIds=..; each model's own licence is read from its metadata and kept with the file (example: 3DPX-022787 human heart, Public Domain, GLB).

tools.name: RCSB Protein Data Bank
tools.notes: Protein structures by PDB id (https://files.rcsb.org/download/<ID>.pdb).

tools.name: PubChem
tools.licence: Public domain (NCBI); a few depositor records carry their own terms
tools.notes: 3D structures (SDF) and properties by compound name or CID; RDKit makes one when PubChem has no 3D record.

tools.name: Schemdraw
tools.notes: Draws circuit schematics as SVG; BIE splits the drawing into one piece per element so the block builds the circuit part by part.

tools.name: Lcapy
tools.notes: Symbolic circuit analysis (SymPy): the exact formula of a circuit's response, used to check ngspice. LGPL: a library BIE calls, not changed.

tools.name: ngspice
tools.licence: BSD-3-Clause (modified BSD; some parts under other free licences)
tools.notes: The SPICE circuit simulator, run in batch mode (transient analysis); from Ubuntu's apt (ngspice 42+ds-3build1 on 24.04). PySpice (GPL, last release 2021) is not used: BIE writes the netlist itself.

tools.name: Python Control Systems Library
tools.notes: Transfer functions, step and frequency responses, step_info (overshoot, settling time).

tools.name: SciPy signal (scipy.signal)
tools.notes: Part of SciPy (same pin): filters, LTI systems; here it checks python-control's step responses.

tools.name: PyNite (PyNiteFEA)
tools.notes: 3D finite-element analysis of frames, beams and plates: deflection, moments, reactions.

tools.name: SymPy physics (sympy.physics)
tools.notes: Part of SymPy (same pin): continuum mechanics (beams), mechanics, units; here its Beam solves the closed form that checks PyNite.

tools.name: CoolProp
tools.notes: Thermophysical properties of water, refrigerants and air: steam tables, cycles, T–s and p–h charts.

tools.name: CadQuery (with OCP, OpenCascade)
tools.licence: Apache-2.0 (CadQuery and the OCP bindings; OpenCascade itself LGPL-2.1 with an exception)
tools.notes: Parametric CAD in Python on the OpenCascade kernel; parts are exported as STL and turned into .glb with trimesh for the 3D blocks. Pins cadquery-ocp 7.9.3.1.1.

tools.name: scikit-fem
tools.notes: Added by Claude in place of FEniCS for the toolbox: pure-Python finite elements (heat, elasticity, potential fields) with a PyPI wheel.

tools.name: FEniCSx (DOLFINx)
tools.blocked_reason: DOLFINx has no PyPI wheel: it installs from conda-forge, Docker or Ubuntu's apt (python3-dolfinx, built for the system Python 3.12), while BIE's toolbox runs on Python 3.13 with pip. Needs a separate conda or Docker lane; scikit-fem covers the textbook finite-element cases meanwhile.
tools.notes: Kept in the registry so the gap is visible; the resolver picks scikit-fem for vector_field.

tools.name: GMT (Generic Mapping Tools)
tools.notes: The map-making engine PyGMT drives; from Ubuntu's apt (gmt, libgmt-dev, gmt-dcw, gmt-gshhg-low, with ghostscript for PNG output).

tools.name: PyGMT
tools.notes: Shaded relief maps and profiles (grdimage, project, grdtrack) rendered to PNG, then animated by BIE's image and camera layers.

tools.name: GMT Earth relief (SRTM15+ V2.7)
tools.version: SRTM15+ V2.7 (GMT remote data, 2 arc-min tiles)
tools.licence: Free to use with citation (Tozer et al., 2019, Scripps); GMT remote data
tools.notes: Downloaded by GMT on first use into GMT_USERDIR inside the asset cache (outside git). No formal licence text; recorded for Navin's licence decision.

tools.name: ObsPy
tools.notes: Seismology: TauP ray paths and travel times through the IASP91 Earth model; reading and filtering seismograms. LGPL: used as a library, not changed.

tools.name: pyGPlates
tools.notes: Plate reconstructions: coastlines rotated back in time with a published plate model.

tools.name: Müller et al. (2019) plate model
tools.notes: Rotation file and coastlines from the GPlates model repository (repo.gplates.org), unpacked once into the asset cache; 250 million years.

tools.name: USGS earthquake catalogue
tools.notes: Earthquakes by date range and magnitude as GeoJSON, kept in the asset library with credit.

tools.name: Natural Earth (world-atlas TopoJSON)
tools.licence: Public domain (Natural Earth data); ISC (the world-atlas package)
tools.notes: Natural Earth 1:110m land and countries, bundled in the toolbox web bundle; drawn with d3-geo (part of D3).

tools.name: topojson-client
tools.notes: Turns world-atlas TopoJSON into GeoJSON features for d3-geo.

tools.name: Astropy
tools.notes: Units, constants, time scales and coordinates; here it checks orbital periods by Kepler's third law and converts local time.

tools.name: Skyfield
tools.notes: Positions of planets, the Moon and stars from JPL ephemerides; altitude and azimuth from any place.

tools.name: JPL ephemeris DE421
tools.notes: 17 MB, fetched once into BIE_ASSET_CACHE/skyfield.

tools.name: Hipparcos star catalogue
tools.licence: Free for scientific use with citation (CDS); commercial use under ESA's rules for the Hipparcos data
tools.notes: 118,218 stars (53 MB), fetched once into BIE_ASSET_CACHE/skyfield; recorded for Navin's licence decision.

tools.name: NASA Image and Video Library
tools.licence: per item (NASA media are generally not copyrighted; some carry third-party rights)
tools.notes: Pictures by NASA id with title, centre and description; an item that names a third-party copyright holder is marked for checking.

tools.name: AeroSandbox
tools.notes: Aircraft geometry (wings with real airfoils, fuselages), meshes, and aerodynamics (vortex lattice method, lift curves).

tools.name: OpenVSP
tools.blocked_reason: OpenVSP is not on PyPI: its Python API ships only inside OpenVSP's own release builds, compiled for one Python version, and there is no Ubuntu apt package. Needs a pinned OpenVSP build in its own lane; AeroSandbox builds aircraft shapes meanwhile.
tools.notes: NASA's parametric aircraft geometry tool; kept in the registry so the gap is visible.

tools.name: JSBSim
tools.notes: Flight dynamics with real aircraft models (Cessna 172, 737 ...) and their autopilots; the wheel ships the aircraft data. LGPL: used as a library.

tools.name: BIE science blocks (bie/brain/video/blocks/toolbox)
tools.block: xy_lines, circuit_build, beam_load, heat_plate, earth_section, world_points, plate_frames, orbits, sky_dome, flight_profile
tools.notes: The batch 2 blocks: they draw what the Python tools compute (D3 and d3-geo inside); every block refuses numbers its two tools disagree on where a check exists (circuit: ngspice against lcapy).

tools.name: Natural Earth 1:10m vector data (GeoJSON)
tools.notes: Countries (with India's own point-of-view boundary file, ne_10m_admin_0_countries_ind), states and provinces, and populated places, fetched once from the v5.1.2 tag and pinned by content hash. A map of India drawn from it must still be checked against the Survey of India's boundary before it is published (Navin's decision).

tools.name: Shapely
tools.notes: Geometry for maps: picks India's states, simplifies them for drawing, keeps neighbours off India's boundary and computes areas (equal-area projection).

tools.name: Wikimedia Commons
tools.licence: per item (public domain, CC BY, CC BY-SA ...; non-commercial and no-derivatives refused)
tools.notes: BIE's asset library already searched Commons (Task 039); batch 3 adds a named file with its own licence, and share-alike pictures are kept and tagged share-alike for Navin's decision. Requests are slowed down when Commons answers 429.

tools.name: Openverse
tools.licence: per item (CC BY, CC BY-SA, CC0, public domain mark; non-commercial and no-derivatives refused)
tools.notes: Openly licensed pictures from Flickr, Wikimedia, museums and more, through one API; the file comes through Openverse's own image proxy.

tools.name: World Bank Indicators API (World Development Indicators)
tools.notes: Any indicator for any countries and years, kept in the asset library with its credit (growth, income, life expectancy, population ...).

tools.name: Chart.js
tools.notes: Bars and lines on a canvas; BIE turns its own animation off and grows the chart frame by frame so every render is the same.

tools.name: Vega-Lite
tools.notes: A chart grammar: BIE writes the spec, Vega-Lite compiles it to Vega.

tools.name: Vega
tools.notes: Renders the compiled chart to SVG headless, once per frame.

tools.name: Plotly.js (plotly.js-dist-min)
tools.notes: Scientific charts (contours, surfaces, heatmaps); drawn as a static plot each frame.

tools.name: Mermaid
tools.notes: Diagrams from text (flowcharts, sequence, mind maps, timelines); BIE renders once and reveals node by node.

tools.name: @mermaid-js/layout-elk
tools.notes: Lets Mermaid lay its diagrams out with ELK (layout: elk).

tools.name: elkjs (Eclipse Layout Kernel)
tools.licence: EPL-2.0 (one of elkjs's two licences; BIE takes EPL-2.0 and does not modify it)
tools.notes: Graph layout. elkjs is offered under EPL-2.0 or a GPL licence; BIE uses it under EPL-2.0, a weak copyleft: changes to elkjs's own files would have to be shared, BIE's code is not affected. Pinned to the 0.9 line that Mermaid's ELK layout asks for.

tools.name: dagre (@dagrejs/dagre)
tools.notes: Layered graph layout for BIE's own flowchart block (steps, decisions, ends, labelled edges).

tools.name: India Code (official repository of Indian law)
tools.licence: Government of India content; Acts may be reproduced (Copyright Act 1957, s. 52(1)(q)) with the source acknowledged
tools.notes: Bare acts as data: an Act's record and every section (number, official title, text) through India Code's open REST API, kept in the cache. Flowcharts find their sections by official title, never by a number typed from memory.

tools.name: Indian Supreme Court Judgments (open dataset)
tools.version: metadata parquet by year (AWS Open Data, updated every two months)
tools.licence: CC BY 4.0 (dataset by Dattam Labs); judgments from the Supreme Court of India
tools.notes: Every Supreme Court judgment since 1950: parties, bench, citations, date, and the PDF in English and Indian languages.

tools.name: Apache Arrow (pyarrow)
tools.notes: Reads Parquet tables (the judgments dataset's metadata).

tools.name: PsychoPy (psychopy.data)
tools.notes: Experiment design (trial lists, randomisation, staircases). Only psychopy.data is used: the lane installs PsychoPy with --no-deps (its own pins need Python below 3.13 and a desktop stack) plus json-tricks 3.17.3 (BSD-3-Clause) and i18next 0.0.3 (MIT). GPL: Navin's decision.

tools.name: Indic NLP Library
tools.notes: Tokenising and akshara (orthographic syllable) splitting for Indian scripts; the two script tables it needs are pinned by hash.

tools.name: indic_transliteration (sanscript)
tools.notes: Devanagari to Roman (IAST, ISO 15919) and between Indian scripts.

tools.name: Noto Sans Devanagari (font)
tools.notes: The script font every render loads from the asset library, so all machines draw the same letters.

tools.name: BIE social-science blocks (bie/brain/video/blocks/toolbox)
tools.block: india_map, timeline_build, mermaid_build, flow_build, tree_build, case_card, chartjs_build, vega_build, plotly_build, kinetic_text, experiment_flow
tools.notes: The batch 3 blocks; a law block shows the section number its data source gives, a chart block grows from the data BIE fetched.

tools.name: Twemoji graphics (jdecked/twemoji)
tools.notes: About 1,900 flat colour icons (people, shops, goods, money, flags; skin-tone variants left out) for the build-up canvas (Task 046 Part C). The index bie/toolbox/icons/index.json.gz is searched by the director; each SVG is fetched one by one from the v16.0.1 tag on GitHub (assets/svg) into the asset cache, never into git. Credit line: 'Twemoji graphics by Twitter, Inc and other contributors, CC BY 4.0' (LICENSE-GRAPHICS; the code is MIT and is not used).

tools.name: Font Awesome Free icons
tools.notes: About 2,300 one-colour line icons (solid and regular styles) with search terms, coloured by BIE at copy time; the brands style is never indexed (no logos in lessons, CV-11). Fetched per file from the 7.3.1 tag of FortAwesome/Font-Awesome (svgs/) into the asset cache. The Free licence: icons CC BY 4.0, fonts OFL, code MIT; only the icon SVGs are used. Credit line: 'Font Awesome Free by Fonticons, Inc., CC BY 4.0'.

tools.name: BIE build-up canvas and world blocks (bie/brain/video/blocks/toolbox/canvas.tsx, world.tsx)
tools.notes: Task 046 Part C, from the economy kit of 27 October 2026. canvas_build: a paper canvas that builds up on the spoken words (text, callouts, icons, crowds that grow and shrink, values that change, arrows, trees, tables, marks, highlights, focus) with L3 touches (shadows, idle motion, walk-ins, goods and coins flowing along arrows, a camera that follows the story): Navin's B level, the default for every economy part. curve_story: a graph that draws itself with dots, shades, guides and notes on cue. world_scene: a 2.5D street with a shop or a bank (the bank kit of PR 3: a teller behind the counter, a board whose value changes), procedural people, price tags, coin rain, a balance and camera keys in world pixels: Navin's C level for story parts. The plans are compiled and checked by bie/brain/canvas.py and bie/brain/video/world.py; captions are drawn once by the core strip.
